ai.literal: Is not fault to him even if, sulking is capable of his bestowing way.
ai.translation: Even when he is entirely without fault, feigning a quarrel has the power to draw out his sweet affection.
ai.modern: அவரிடம் எந்தத் தவறும் இல்லை என்றாலும், அவர் அன்பை வெளிப்படுத்தும் விதத்தைக் காண ஊடுதல் வல்லமை உடையது.
ai.explanation: The speaker notes that her lover has committed no actual fault to justify her anger. However, she still engages in a feigned quarrel because it prompts him to soothe her. This playful sulking is powerful because it reveals the beautiful and tender way he shows his love to win her back.

ai.literal: From the lovers' quarrel appearing small distress, good affection even if it fades, greatness will get.
ai.translation: The slight distress that arises from a lovers' quarrel brings a sweet reward, even if it makes their good affection seem to fade.
ai.modern: காதலர்களிடையே ஏற்படும் ஊடலால் தோன்றும் சிறிய துன்பம், அவர்களின் நல்ல அன்பினைச் சிறிது நேரம் வாடச் செய்தாலும், முடிவில் இன்பம் என்னும் பெருமையைப் பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explores the emotional value of a lovers' quarrel. The word 'ஊடல்' refers to the feigned anger or sulking between lovers, which causes a 'சிறுதுனி' or slight distress. Although this temporary distress might make their deep affection ('அளி') seem to fade ('வாடினும்') for a moment, it ultimately brings a greater sweetness or value ('பாடு') to their relationship when they reunite. The contrast between the temporary fading of affection and the gaining of greatness highlights how such quarrels only serve to strengthen love.

ai.literal: Than sulking, celestial land is there? with earth water having blended those who are like - in the heart.
ai.translation: Is there a heaven sweeter than the lovers' sulking, when their hearts are blended like water with the earth?
ai.modern: நிலத்தோடு நீர் கலந்திருப்பதைப் போல அன்பால் கலந்த காதலர்களின் நெஞ்சத்தில் தோன்றும் ஊடலை விட இன்பமான தேவர் உலகம் வேறு இருக்கிறதா?
ai.explanation: The couplet compares the union of lovers to the blending of water with the earth, an inseparable and natural bond. It asks whether even the celestial world of the gods could offer a joy greater than the lovers' feigned anger (sulking). The word 'புலத்தல்' refers to this delicate, temporary sulking that only deepens their affection. The imagery of earth and water highlights how their hearts are completely absorbed in each other.

ai.literal: Having embraced, not letting go, in the feigned anger appears my heart-breaking weapon.
ai.translation: In her feigned anger, where she embraces me and refuses to let go, there appears a weapon that shatters my heart.
ai.modern: என்னைத் தழுவிக்கொண்டு விடாமல் இருக்கும் அவளது ஊடலில், என் நெஞ்சின் உறுதியை உடைக்கும் ஒரு படைக்கருவி தோன்றுகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes the captivating nature of his lover's feigned anger. Even while sulking, she embraces him and refuses to let go. Within this tender contradiction of anger and affection, he sees a 'weapon'—her captivating charm—that completely shatters his own heart's resolve. The word 'படை' (weapon) beautifully captures how her sulking conquers his mind.

ai.literal: Faultless they are even if, oneself-loved ones' soft shoulders from separating, there one thing it has.
ai.translation: Even when there is no fault, stepping away from the soft shoulders of one's beloved holds a certain sweet charm.
ai.modern: காதலர்கள் மீது எந்தத் தவறும் இல்லை என்றாலும், தாம் விரும்பும் காதலியின் மென்மையான தோள்களை விட்டுச் சற்று விலகி ஊடுவதில் ஒரு தனி இன்பம் இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the paradoxical joy of a lovers' quarrel. The speaker notes that even when neither partner has committed any fault, feigning a quarrel and stepping away from the beloved's soft embrace brings its own unique pleasure. The phrase 'one thing it has' delicately hints at the sweet anticipation of reuniting after a brief, playful separation.

ai.literal: Even than eating, what was eaten digesting is sweet; in love, than uniting, sulking is sweet.
ai.translation: Digesting what one has eaten is even more pleasant than the act of eating. Likewise, in love, a feigned quarrel is sweeter than the union itself.
ai.modern: உண்பதை விட உண்ட உணவு செரிப்பது உடலுக்கு அதிக இன்பம் தரும். அதுபோலவே, காதலில் கூடி மகிழ்வதை விட ஊடல் கொள்வது அதிக இன்பம் தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a striking parallel between physical digestion and romantic relationships. The poet states that the digestion of food brings more comfort and pleasure to the body than the act of eating itself. Similarly, in romantic love, the playful sulking or feigned quarrel is sweeter than the actual physical union. The comparison suggests that just as digestion prepares the body to enjoy the next meal, a lovers' quarrel renews their desire and makes their subsequent reunion much more delightful.

ai.literal: In lovers' quarrel, those who lost won; that indeed in union will be seen.
ai.translation: Those who lose in a lovers' quarrel are the true winners. That truth will be seen in the joy of their reunion.
ai.modern: காதலர் ஊடலில் தோற்றவரே உண்மையில் வெற்றி பெற்றவர் ஆவார்; அந்த உண்மை அவர்கள் கூடி மகிழும்போது வெளிப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet reveals the paradox of a lovers' quarrel. The one who yields and 'loses' the argument actually wins, because yielding brings the quarrel to an end and leads to the joy of reunion. The word 'தோற்றவர்' (those who lost) is contrasted with 'வென்றார்' (they won) to highlight this irony. The sweetness of the resulting 'கூடல்' (union) proves that losing the quarrel was the true victory.

ai.literal: Having sulked, will we get, I wonder, forehead to sweat, in union appeared delight?
ai.translation: I wonder if we can attain by sulking again that sweet delight which arose in our union, making our foreheads sweat.
ai.modern: நெற்றி வியர்க்கும்படி நாம் கூடியபோது உண்டான அந்த இன்பத்தை, மீண்டும் ஊடல் கொள்வதன் மூலம் நாம் பெறுவோமா?
ai.explanation: The couplet captures a lover's reflection on the intense joy of physical union following a lovers' tiff. The lover remembers how their recent reconciliation was so passionate that their foreheads broke into a sweat. The word 'உப்பு' literally means salt, but here it signifies the 'flavor' or 'delight' that enhances love. Having experienced this heightened pleasure, the lover wonders if feigning another quarrel will once again yield such a sweet reward.

ai.literal: Let sulk oh that, bright jewel, we to beg; let lengthen oh that, night.
ai.translation: Let the brightly jeweled woman feign anger so I may plead with her, and let the night stretch on to give us time.
ai.modern: ஒளிரும் அணிகலன்களை அணிந்தவள் என்னோடு ஊடல் கொள்வாளாக; அவளிடம் நான் கெஞ்சி இரந்து நிற்பதற்காக இந்த இரவு இன்னும் நீள்வதாக.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses a deep delight in the lover's feigned quarrel. He wishes that the woman, described metonymically by her bright jewels, would continue to sulk so that he can have the pleasure of pleading with her. To fully enjoy this sweet process of appeasing her, he wishes for the night to stretch on and last longer. The optative verbs 'ūṭuka' (let her sulk) and 'nīṭuka' (let it lengthen) highlight his active desire for this playful conflict and the time to resolve it.

ai.literal: Feigning anger to passion is joy; to that is joy, having united to embrace if obtained.
ai.translation: A lovers' quarrel is the joy of love, and the joy of that quarrel is the close embrace when they reunite.
ai.modern: காதலுக்கு இன்பம் தருவது ஊடல் ஆகும். அந்த ஊடலுக்கு இன்பம் தருவது, ஊடல் தீர்ந்து இருவரும் கூடித் தழுவுவதைப் பெறுவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet concludes the Tirukkural by celebrating the playful conflicts between lovers. It states that feigning anger adds delight to romantic passion. Furthermore, the true joy of such a quarrel is realized only when it ends in a warm, reconciling embrace. The progression from passion to quarrel and finally to embrace highlights how temporary separation heightens the pleasure of reunion.
